views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Use the Osaka G20 meeting to reopen talks and seek a Buenos Aires-style freeze: no $300B List 4 tariffs, a pause in further entity-list expansion, and a return to working-level text without new structural or purchase commitments. Keep the unreliable-entity list and rare-earth signaling as unused leverage; do not populate the list or cut rare-earth exports on the eve of the summit. Do not unilaterally roll back the June 1 tariff hike or concede enforcement language the US claimed we walked back in May.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. After May 10 the US is already taxing ~$250B of our goods at 25%, and on May 16 Commerce put Huawei and affiliates on the Entity List; Google, Qualcomm and other US suppliers then cut Android/GMS and chips — a direct hit on our leading telecom/smartphone champion and on Made-in-China 2025 (timeline 2019-05-10, 2019-05-16, 2019-05-20). Official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.4 in May, new export orders to 46.5, and the employment sub-index to 47.0, the weakest since March 2009; April IP (5.4%) and retail sales (7.2%, slowest in 16 years) already showed the earlier stimulus rebound fading. That maps to the CHN +0.5 anchor (export-sector damage, Huawei targeting, unemployment risk in export hubs). It is not +1.0: services PMI remains in expansion, March data showed stimulus can stabilize activity, and there is no visible financial-stability break. The residual opportunity (nationalist rally, faster tech autonomy, rare-earth leverage via Xi’s May 20 Jiangxi visit) is real but does not offset the tariff-plus-tech squeeze, so the net reading is +0.55 rather than negative.

Action should be negotiate, not escalate or concede. Trump has said he will decide the remaining ~$300B (phones, computers, clothing) after meeting Xi; Mnuchin has framed Osaka as analogous to Buenos Aires. Populating the unreliable-entity list or restricting rare earths now would give Washington a pretext to impose List 4 and deepen the Huawei cutoff — a second-order hit we cannot easily absorb given May factory and employment readings. Conversely, purchase or structural concessions before any US tariff freeze or Huawei relief would validate the May 5 “renegotiate” accusation and look like capitulation after a national-champion assault. Teams are already in contact to “consolidate the consensus” from the June 18 call. The disciplined stance is therefore near-zero on the escalate–concede axis: talk, freeze further damage, keep counters unused.
key_factors: US List 3 already at 25% on ~$200B plus $50B earlier lists; remaining ~$300B threatened after Osaka
Huawei Entity List plus Google/chip cutoff — firm-level tech assault, not just tariffs
May official PMI 49.4, export orders 46.5, manufacturing employment 47.0 (weakest since 2009)
G20 Osaka (28–29 Jun) is the first Trump-Xi meeting since the May collapse; US has tied List 4 to the meeting outcome
China already retaliated on ~$60B (1 Jun) and announced but has not implemented an unreliable-entity list — unused leverage
Talks previously stalled on enforcement/IP/tech-transfer, not just purchases; unilateral purchase concessions would be premature

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
Google suspends Huawei's access to Android updates / GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales. Same day: Xi Jinping visits a rare-earth facility in Jiangxi.
China announces it will establish an "unreliable entity list" targeting foreign firms that cut supplies to Chinese companies for non-commercial reasons.
Trump and Xi agree by phone to meet at the G20 in Osaka.
Trump ... Orders List 3 raised from 10% to 25% on May 10 and directs preparation of tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (~$300B).
Official PMI fell to 49.4 in May from 50.1; export orders pulled back to 46.5 from 49.2; factory activity slump heaps pressure for more stimulus.
May manufacturing PMI 49.4; employment sub-index 47.0, lowest since March 2009; new orders 49.8 from 51.4.
Trump preparing 25% tariffs on remaining ~$300B of Chinese imports; Mnuchin says Osaka has parallels to Buenos Aires; Huawei sanctions described as separate.
First Trump-Xi meeting since May breakdown; experts expect at best a halt to further escalation and resumed negotiations, not a substantive deal.
US 10-year yield 2.05 on 2019-06-26 vs 2.69 at end-2018 (−24%), consistent with a growth/trade-war risk-off that also constrains China’s external demand.
